anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U4 and U12 have both their isolated-side and logic-side ground pins (GND1 and GND2) connected to the same main GND net. U4/U12 VCC2 is also supplied from 5V_switched_CAN, which is derived from the main +5V rail rather than an isolated supply.
anomalies.expected: For an isolated CAN bus, GND1 and GND2 must be separate ground nets (or at least the bus side must have an isolated ground and isolated supply). The specification describes two isolated CAN buses driven through isolated CAN transceivers.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The CAN transceivers are not galvanically isolated as intended. This can allow ground loops and motor-side common-mode currents to couple into the logic/compute ground, defeating the stated isolated CAN architecture.

parsed.summary: The design files show isolated CAN transceivers U4 and U12 with GND1 and GND2 both tied to the main GND, contradicting the specification's intended isolated CAN buses and removing the isolation barrier.
